gap: No result ChatGPT got states, side by side for each 140 W-class charger, what the MacBook's port keeps once a second device is plugged in, nor Notebookcheck's 56–58 W reading on the UGREEN Nexode Pro 160W 5-Port's C1 port with four other devices charging.
standout_why: Compared against thegadgetmasters.com (cited), Macworld (cited), Apple Support 102378 (cited), thisusb.com, specsource.org, thunderboltlaptop.com, verdictbits.com and compatwiki.com. thisusb.com already prints the core line for ChatGPT's pick (Anker A2697: Mac plus phone gives 100 W + 40 W, 'below the 140W line'). Macworld prints partial splits (Anker A2697 134 W across four devices, Baseus PicoGo two laptops at 70 W each, Nexode Pro 160W 4-port 65 + 65 W). thegadgetmasters, specsource, thunderboltlaptop and compatwiki give single-port maximums only and say shared power 'decreases' without watts. None carries a shared-load figure for the 5-port Nexode Pro 160W, AOHi The Youth or Anker Prime 160W. The new part is therefore the cross-charger table and the Notebookcheck reading, not the idea itself.
decides: For a shopper who charges only the MacBook, every candidate meets 140 W on its maker's figure, so the angle does not separate them. If a phone shares the charger, ChatGPT's pick (Anker A2697, 140 W total) drops the Mac to 100 W, and AOHi The Youth drops to 65 W; both fall below Apple's 140 W fast-charge line. The 160 W-total chargers (UGREEN Nexode Pro 160W 5-Port, Anker Prime 160W) have 20 W of arithmetic room above 140 W, but neither maker's page I could open prints the two-port split, so the page must not claim they 'keep 140 W' with a phone attached. Anker says only '160W Max' for two ports. For UGREEN, the only shared-load figure is Notebookcheck's 56–58 W on C1 with all five ports busy. This confirms the map's lean toward a 160 W unit over a 140 W-total one, with the footnote that only Apple's single-port adapter has nothing to share. One naming trap also matters: three different products are sold as 'Nexode Pro 160W'. Macworld reviews the 4-port (one 140 W port, 304 g), thegadgetmasters describes the retractable-cable one, and ours is the 5-port X774 (two 140 W ports, 353–360 g).
